changes.before: Add byrow=TRUE when creating the matrix. What prints?
changes.after: A matrix arranges values into rows and columns. By default R fills one column before moving to the next.

before: matrix(c(1,2,3,4), nrow=2) creates a two-row matrix. An array generalizes dimensions beyond rows and columns.
With byrow=FALSE, the first column receives 1 and 2, then the second receives 3 and 4. byrow=TRUE fills rows instead.
m[1,2] reads row 1, column 2. Changing the fill order changes where input values are placed, not the meaning of the two indices.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
m <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), nrow=2)
cat(m[1, 2])
```
